purpose: One private account per person for money, shared expenses, groceries, meals and nutrition, workouts, body measurements, tasks and a calendar, with an assistant that works on the same data.
users: Many people, each with their own private data (health data is never shared or published). Nothing in the interface assumes a particular person.
source_of_truth: docs/design-system/PURPLE_MAIN_THEME.md (the Purple Main Theme: the full specification of the look, every token and component)
frontend/src/theme/orchid.css (the Money, Settings and Profile scope)
frontend/src/index.css (colour tokens, contrast floor, glass, motion)
frontend/tailwind.config.js (how the tokens become Tailwind colours, radii, fonts)
frontend/e2e/a11y-*.spec.js and frontend/e2e/mobile-nav.spec.js (the rules below, enforced)

colour_tokens_hsl.note: Values are HSL components exactly as written in index.css; Tailwind exposes them as bg-background, text-foreground, bg-card, text-muted-foreground, border-border, bg-primary, ...

contrast_floor.rule: Text must reach WCAG AA (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large). Secondary text is written as text-slate-400/500 across the app, so the floor is applied once, in index.css, instead of in every class list.
contrast_floor.buttons_with_white_text: The default Button (bg-primary: white on it is 6.75:1 in the light theme and 5.86:1 in the dark one). The emerald and teal classes are the orchid ramp now; a gain, a warning or a success is written green, red or amber.
contrast_floor.text_in_a_data_colour: Use the tint-text class with a --tint style variable (a category, a workout type). It darkens the colour in the light theme and lightens it in the dark theme until it reads on its own pale tint. The raw colour stays for dots, bars and icons.
contrast_floor.how_to_change_it: Add a colour to the floor only when the audit finds it failing; explicit dark:, hover: and focus: classes on the same element still win (the selectors use :where()).

typography.sans: Plus Jakarta Sans, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif
typography.mono: JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, monospace (code and the assistant's inline amounts only: lm-money). Figures use the same face as the words, in tabular numerals (stat-num).
typography.amount_in_a_stat_card: text-xl sm:text-3xl font-extrabold; a word in a stat card (a category name) is set as text, text-base sm:text-lg, or it outgrows the card
typography.label: a small muted label via the Label component (text-xs, semibold); no uppercase text anywhere

surfaces.card: card-ambient: 24px radius, the --card-fill gradient, a --line hairline and the --card-edge shadow (a light top edge and a long soft drop); the Card component in common.jsx
surfaces.glass: only for layers that float above content: the top bar (glass), the phone bottom bar (glass-strong), the assistant button and panel
surfaces.dialogs: Radix Dialog via components/ui/dialog.jsx; the close button is at least 24 by 24 px; every dialog has a title and a (possibly screen-reader-only) description
surfaces.sheets: components/ui/sheet.jsx (the phone's More sheet); focus returns to the control that opened it

layout_and_navigation.desktop: Left sidebar with all pages (lg and up), top bar with search/command (Ctrl or Cmd + K), theme switch and Add
layout_and_navigation.phone: Bottom bar: Home, Money, + (quick add), People, Tasks, More. More opens a sheet with the other pages and Sign out, so every page is two taps away (derived from the NAV list, so a new page cannot be unreachable).
layout_and_navigation.current_page: aria-current="page" on the active link; the More tab carries it when the current page is inside the sheet
layout_and_navigation.no_horizontal_scroll: No page scrolls sideways at 390, 820 or 1280 px; headings and toolbars wrap (SectionHeading wraps its action), and long words are set as text rather than as large amounts

accessibility_rules.enforced_by: frontend/e2e/a11y-pages.spec.js, a11y-public.spec.js, a11y-empty-states.spec.js, nutrition-a11y.spec.js (axe-core, WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2, levels A and AA, at 1280, 820 and 390 px in both themes) and mobile-nav.spec.js
accessibility_rules.names: Every control has an accessible name. Icon-only buttons need aria-label; Select triggers need aria-label or a linked label; checkboxes in lists name their row ("Select Marta").
accessibility_rules.label_in_name: A button's accessible name must contain its visible text (WCAG 2.5.3). Let the name come from the content and add a screen-reader-only part for extra detail.
accessibility_rules.target_size: At least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8); give icon buttons shrink-0 so a flex row cannot squeeze them.
accessibility_rules.forms: Visible labels are linked with htmlFor/id; errors are inline text with role="alert" next to the field, not only a toast.
accessibility_rules.empty_states: A new account has data nowhere; every page has an empty state that is audited too (the Money page offers 'Set up your money').
accessibility_rules.exceptions: The grocery catalog (about 500 cards) is audited at the full document height with the assistant button and bottom bar hidden: at any one scroll position some cards sit under those fixed controls or straddle the window's edge, which axe reports as 'partially obscured'.

motion.principle: Short and calm. Entrance fades, no layout-moving animation.
motion.respect_the_user: Honour prefers-reduced-motion everywhere, and the in-app Animations switch (Settings). Page transitions and the typing indicator already do; see the MotionConfig at the app root for framer-motion.
motion.no_universal_transition: Never transition: all. Name the properties.

feedback.toasts: Sonner (components/ui/sonner.jsx) for confirmations and errors that are not tied to one field
feedback.loading: Skeleton placeholders (the skeleton class) while data arrives; never an empty state for data that is on its way
feedback.errors: A plain sentence the person can act on. Server errors arrive as JSON with a detail; the page shows it and does not call itself offline unless nothing answered (docs/testing/failure-sweep.md)
feedback.limits: 429 answers carry a plain message and Retry-After (README, Usage limits)

testing_conventions.data_testid: Every interactive element has a data-testid in kebab-case that says what it is (expense-save, mnav-more, onboarding-create)
testing_conventions.browser_specs: frontend/e2e, run with `python backend/tests/isolated_env.py run -- npx playwright test` against a throw-away stack; specs that call a live model are named 'real assistant' or 'real model' and are never part of the automated run

privacy_in_the_interface.health_data: Never shown on a shareable link, never emailed in a report unless the person chose the recipient and confirmed it
privacy_in_the_interface.account: Settings, 'Your data': download everything, or delete the account after the password and an exact confirmation phrase
